title: CPG & retail supplier procurement → Floras
floras_mechanism: For consumer goods, retail, and food & beverage companies with large supplier networks, Floras embeds a small climate contribution into qualifying procurement transactions. Suppliers integrate Floras into invoices or product lines; the buyer accumulates Floras in an enterprise wallet tied to purchasing activity. The buyer allocates those Floras toward verified sustainability projects—with certificates documenting impact for Scope 3, ESG, and supplier engagement reporting.
pain_signals: Scope 3 emissions dominate footprint from purchased goods and services
hundreds or thousands of suppliers with limited sustainability participation
supplier sustainability data is poor or incomplete
ESG pressure on supply chain decarbonization
difficulty scaling climate action across procurement volume
sustainability team lacks leverage over day-to-day purchasing
budget_source: Procurement budget; supplier development budget; ESG and Scope 3 program budget; supplier-embedded climate contributions on qualifying transactions
safe_claims: Floras links climate-designated value to procurement transactions rather than treating climate funding as a separate annual purchase
Enterprises collect Floras in a wallet from supplier-integrated transactions and allocate them toward verified projects
Floras can support supplier engagement by embedding climate value into the purchasing relationship
Companies receive certificates documenting supported projects for ESG and stakeholder reporting
Climate action scales with procurement volume because Floras accumulate from transactions
conditional_claims: If the company has published Scope 3 or supplier decarbonization targets, Floras can align wallet allocation with those priorities
If key suppliers are willing to integrate, Floras can start with a pilot category before broad rollout
If the company tracks supplier-level sustainability, Floras can complement engagement programs with transaction-linked funding
avoid_claims: Floras automatically reduces all Scope 3 emissions
Every supplier becomes sustainable by integrating Floras
Floras replaces supplier audits, traceability, or material reduction strategies
Procurement spend is carbon-neutral once Floras is attached

output_templates.one_liner: Turn {company_name}'s supplier spend into verified climate action at procurement scale.
output_templates.short_pitch: {company_name} manages high-volume procurement across a large supplier base—exactly where Scope 3 pressure concentrates. Floras embeds a small climate contribution into qualifying supplier transactions so value flows into an enterprise wallet instead of sitting outside day-to-day purchasing. Your team can allocate those Floras toward verified projects and receive certificates that connect procurement activity to funded climate impact for ESG and supplier engagement narratives.

objections_and_responses.objection: We already run supplier sustainability surveys and annual offset purchases.
objections_and_responses.response: Floras does not replace surveys or thoughtful climate procurement—it connects funding to the transactions that drive Scope 3. The wallet shows which purchasing activity generated value and what projects were supported, rather than treating climate spend as disconnected from procurement.

objections_and_responses.objection: Our suppliers won't adopt another platform or fee.
objections_and_responses.response: Floras is designed to embed into existing supplier relationships and invoice flows. Pilots can start with willing strategic suppliers or a single category before broader rollout, reducing change-management risk.

objections_and_responses.objection: Scope 3 is too complex—we mostly use estimates.
objections_and_responses.response: Transaction-linked Floras give procurement a concrete engagement lever while sustainability teams improve data coverage over time. It turns purchasing behavior into measurable climate funding without claiming full Scope 3 accuracy on day one.
